_comment: Townsfolk. occupations: where they are found (building kind, 'street' or 'stall'), title per settlement kind where it differs, notable (gets a full profile, AI-written when possible), social class (low/middle/high), purse in copper [min, max], stats (a creature id used if it comes to a fight), trade (what they sell, see economy.json), services (see economy.json). personality: traits with their effect on first impressions (disposition), bribes and threats. Text tables fill the built-in profiles; {slots} are filled by code.

hair_old: grey hair thinning at the crown
white hair and a white beard
a bald head spotted with age
feature: a nose that has been broken more than once
old pox scars across both cheeks
a burn scar up one arm
a cough that never quite stops
a face that has had too much sun
clothes_low: clothes that have been mended past the point of sense
clothes_middle: a clean linen shirt and a leather apron
a dyed tunic, a little faded
sober dark clothes of decent cloth
clothes_high: a fur-trimmed cloak and rings on three fingers
fine black wool and a gold chain
appearance: You notice {feature} first; then the rest: {build}, with {hair}, in {clothes}.
backstory_innkeeper: Took over the inn when {their} father drank himself into the churchyard.
Came here as a serving hand twenty years ago and married the owner's child.
Bought the inn with money nobody asks about.
backstory_priest: Sent here by the temple after some trouble in a bigger place that nobody discusses.
Born in this parish, and has buried half of it.
Took orders after a fever took {their} whole family.
backstory_smith: Learned the trade from {their} mother, who learned it from hers.
Spent ten years making spearheads for an army, and does not talk about it.
Came from the mountains with nothing but a hammer.
backstory_shopkeeper: Started with a handcart and now owns the building.
Inherited the shop and the debts that came with it.
Used to be a pedlar; has walked every road in the region.
backstory_healer: Learned herb-lore from a wise-woman who was later hanged for it.
Was an army surgeon until the smell of the field tents became too much.
backstory_stablemaster: Has worked with horses since {they} could walk.
Was a cavalry groom until the war ended.
Won the stable in a game of dice, or so {they} tell{s} it.
backstory_headman: Chosen because nobody else wanted the job.
The richest farmer hereabouts, which is not saying much.
Has held the office for twenty years and knows every quarrel in the place.
backstory_lord: The second son who inherited when the first died of a winter fever.
Holds these lands from a greater lord and never forgets it.
Came to the title young and has kept it by being careful.
backstory_guard: Joined the watch because it was that or the fields.
An old soldier who never went home.
Took the job for the free boots.
backstory_common: Born here, and will die here, most likely.
Came here after the last bad harvest drove {them} off {their} own land.
Has worked the same ground as {their} father did, and his father before him.
Lost a spouse to the flux two winters ago and has not been the same since.
Owes money to half the town and favours to the other half.
Buried two children and raised three, and does not talk about the first two.
Walked here from the far side of the realm with {their} whole life on {their} back, and stopped because {their} feet did.
Married a soldier who did not come back from the last war.
Has never once been farther than the next village.
Came through the plague year that took most of the street.
Keeps bees, and a grudge against the neighbours, and tends both with care.
Came into a little money once and drank it, and is still sorry.
Was sold into service in a bigger house as a child, and ran.
backstory_farmer: Works a strip of the lord's land and a strip of {their} own, and the lord's comes first.
Lost the last harvest to rain and the one before it to soldiers.
Has ploughed the same field for thirty years and knows every stone in it.
Took on {their} dead brother's land, and {their} dead brother's debts with it.
backstory_labourer: Carries whatever anyone pays to have carried, and has the back to show for it.
Came in from the country when the farm could not feed another mouth.
Dug graves through the plague year, and nobody has shaken {their} hand since.
backstory_weaver: Learned the loom at six and has not been far from one since.
Sells cloth to a merchant who sells it on for three times the price, and knows it.
Weaves for the lord's household and is paid when the steward remembers.
backstory_carter: Has driven every road for a week in any direction, and been robbed on most of them.
Lost a cart and a horse to bandits last year, and bought new ones on credit.
Carries anything, asks nothing, and is paid a little extra for both.
backstory_washerwoman: Washes the linen of half the town and knows its secrets, most of them by the stains.
Was a lady's maid until the lady died, and nobody wanted {them} after.
Raised four children on what the river and a washboard bring in.
backstory_beggar: Had a trade once, and a family, and a roof, and lost them in the other order.
Lost a leg in a war nobody here remembers the reason for.
Was turned off {their} land for a debt {they} never saw written down.
Has sat by this gate so long that the guards say good morning.
backstory_fisher: Fishes the same water as {their} father did, and it gives less every year.
Lost a boat and a brother to the same storm.
Knows every snag and pool for a mile of water, and nothing about anything else.
backstory_woodcutter: Cuts the lord's timber for a wage, and takes a little of the lord's deer for supper.
Has spent more nights in the forest than in a bed.
Was pinned by a falling tree years ago, and still walks bent to one side.
backstory_miner: Went down the pit at nine years old and came up coughing at forty.
Was buried for two days in a fall, and has not been afraid of anything since.
Digs for a master who has never once been below ground.
backstory_market_trader: Buys cheap at dawn from the farms and sells dear by noon to the town.
Has a stall that was {their} mother's and a tongue that was {their} father's.
Was a pedlar on the roads until the roads got too dangerous.
backstory_serving_hand: Came to the inn as a child and has never had wages that were not owed.
Serves ale by day and remembers what the drinkers say by night.
Ran from a hard master in another town, and does not say which.
backstory_acolyte: Was given to the temple by a family that could not feed {them}.
Took vows after a fever that should have killed {them}.
Is learning the prayers and the politics of the temple, in that order.
moments: A woman beats a rug against a wall, and the dust hangs in the light.
Two children are throwing stones at a third, who is not running away.
A dog carries something down an alley at a trot, and does not want to be asked about it.
Somebody is shouting at somebody else behind a shutter. It stops when you pass.
A cart goes by with a broken wheel, going slowly, with a man walking beside it saying nothing.
An old man sits in a doorway with his face turned to what sun there is.
A girl runs past with a live hen under each arm.
Two men are standing very close together and talking very quietly. They stop.
Somebody has been sick in the gutter, and somebody else has thrown ash over it.
A woman sings while she works, badly, and does not care who hears.
A dog follows you for three streets, then loses interest all at once.
Two men are carrying a door somewhere, and neither of them is happy about it.
A woman leans out of an upper window and empties something into the street without looking.
An argument about money is going on behind a shutter, in whispers, which is worse.
Somebody has chalked a crude drawing on a wall, and somebody else has half scrubbed it off.
A boy runs past with bread under his coat and does not look at you.
moments_day: The smith's hammer goes on and on, and the whole street has stopped hearing it.
A pedlar is telling a knot of people about a remedy. Nobody is buying, but nobody leaves.
Washing hangs across the street, and you walk through it.
A carter is arguing about the price of turnips as if his life turned on it, and perhaps it does.
Somebody's pig has got out. Three people are chasing it, and losing.
A cart is being unloaded and everybody is shouting different instructions.
Two apprentices are fighting over something small and their master is enjoying it.
A cat lies in the one patch of sun and refuses to be moved for the traffic.
Somebody is being measured for a coffin, standing up, and taking it well.
moments_night: A shutter opens above you, and closes again quickly.
Somewhere out of sight, a woman is crying, steadily, the way people do when nobody is listening.
The watch goes by with a lantern, and looks at you for a long moment.
A drunk is asleep in a doorway with his hands inside his coat.
A cat crosses the street with its ears back, and something follows it that you do not see.
A watchman goes by with a lantern and looks at you a moment too long.
Two people are saying goodbye in a doorway and have been for some time.
A drunk is explaining something urgent to a wall.
Somewhere a shutter bangs, over and over, and nobody gets up to fix it.
moments_plague: A door is marked with chalk, and nobody walks on that side of the street.
The dead-cart goes by. The driver has a cloth over his face and does not look at anyone.
Somebody is burning herbs in a doorway, which they believe will help.
A priest is going house to house and getting slower as he goes.
Somebody has left food on a doorstep and knocked and walked away.
The church bell has been rung so often for the dead that they have stopped counting.
A woman washes her hands in the trough again and again, long past clean.
moments_famine: A queue at a baker's door, and a man at the front arguing about weight.
Children are stripping the bark off a lime tree, and their mother is helping them.
The bakers' shutters are down at noon and there is a crowd anyway.
Somebody is boiling something in the street that does not smell like food.
A dog goes by thin enough to count, and nobody chases it away.
Two men are arguing over a sack, and both of them are too weak to make it a fight.
moments_raided: A man is nailing a new shutter over a window that has no glass left in it.
Two women are counting what is left in a store shed, twice, hoping for a different answer.
A burnt beam has been dragged into the street and left there.
Somebody is reading out a list of names, and people are waiting to hear their own.
The smith is making nothing but door bars this week.
A child is asking where somebody is, and being told to go inside.
moments_siege: Soldiers are pulling down a shed for the timber, and the owner is watching.
Everyone walks quickly, and nobody looks at the walls.
Water is being carried in and nobody is spilling any.
A man on the wall is pointing something out to another man, who will not look.
The horses have been taken somewhere, and the stables are full of people.
Somebody is sharpening things for anyone who brings them, and not charging.
moments_market: The square is full: stalls, shouting, a fiddler nobody asked for, and the smell of frying.
A farmer is holding a goat by one horn and a purse in the other, deciding.
A man is selling relics: three saints' fingers, all from the same hand.
A crowd has formed round a fight that has not started yet.
Somebody's goose gets loose and the whole row of stalls joins in.
A girl with a tray of pies works the queue and takes no refusals.
